findings.title: Error IDs are zipped against unordered nodestore results
findings.body: `fetch_error_details()` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` and then pairs them with `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. `get_multi()` returns a mapping keyed by node id; its iteration order is an implementation detail (several backends merge cache hits and DB fetches into a new dict), so `events.values()` is not guaranteed to be in the same order as `error_ids`. Worse, missing events are filtered with `if data is not None` *after* zipping, so a single missing event shifts every subsequent pairing. The result is `ErrorEvent.id` values attached to the wrong title/message/timestamp, which is then fed to Seer for summarization. Pair explicitly instead, e.g. iterate `for error_id, node_id in zip(error_ids, node_ids)` and look up `events.get(node_id)`.

findings.title: Error/breadcrumb merge compares timestamps in different units
findings.body: `gen_request_data()` interleaves errors and replay events with `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`. The error timestamps come from the nodestore event payload (epoch **seconds**, e.g. 1.75e9), while the top-level timestamp of an rrweb replay event is epoch **milliseconds** (e.g. 1.75e12). The comparison is therefore always true for real data, so every error is emitted before the first breadcrumb instead of being interleaved chronologically, defeating the purpose of the merge. The new unit tests use hand-written second-based event timestamps (1.5, 2.0), which hides the mismatch. Normalize both sides to the same unit before comparing.

findings.title: Feature-flagged table widget renders hardcoded empty data
findings.body: When `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` is true, the widget renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />`, completely ignoring the `result` that was just fetched. Any organization with this flag enabled will see every dashboard table widget render as an empty table with no columns and no rows, with no error or loading state to explain it. Either wire the real `result`/`fields` into the new component or keep the branch out of the shipped code path.

findings.title: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validation is incomplete and falsy-sensitive
findings.body: The serializer is meant to accept exactly one of `age` (Editor's Draft) or `timestamp` (Working Draft), but: (1) both fields are `required=False` with no object-level check, so a report containing *neither* passes validation; and (2) the cross-checks use truthiness (`if self.initial_data.get("age")` / `.get("timestamp")`), so `age: 0` (a perfectly valid age for a freshly generated report) or `timestamp: 0` bypasses the mutual-exclusion check and both fields are accepted together. Use `is not None` checks and add a `validate()` that requires exactly one of the two fields.

findings.title: get_environment_info triggers a recommended-event lookup per issue in PR comments
findings.body: `get_environment_info()` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` for every issue included in a merged-PR comment. That helper runs a Snuba query plus a nodestore fetch per issue, so building a comment for the top 5 issues now issues up to 5 extra event lookups (each able to time out or return a stale 'recommended' event) inside the PR comment task, for a single word of decoration in the comment. Consider resolving environments from data already fetched (e.g. the group's environments or the snuba row) instead of fetching full events. Also note the `except Exception` branch logs the raw exception object in `extra={"error": e}`; `str(e)` serializes more reliably.

findings.title: Issue list template produces blank lines and a trailing newline in PR comments
findings.body:
`MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE` ends with `
`, but both the GitHub and GitLab workflows join the rendered entries with `"
".join(...)`. Every bullet is therefore separated by a blank line (which Markdown renders as a 'loose' list with extra paragraph spacing) and the list ends with an extra newline immediately before the `<sub>Did you find this useful?</sub>` footer. The updated tests encode this double spacing, so the formatting regression will ship silently. Drop the trailing `
` from the template.

findings.title: Hook now returns possibly-undefined attributes instead of an empty TagCollection
findings.body: Previously `attributes` was derived through a `useMemo` that always produced a `TagCollection` object (`{}` when there was no data). Now it is `isFetching ? previous : data`, where both `previous` (first render) and `data` (query disabled or not yet resolved) are `undefined`. Callers that are not updated in this PR and treat the value as always-present (spreading is fine, but `Object.keys(attributes)` / `attributes[key]` is not) can now hit runtime errors, in particular when the hook is used with `enabled: false`. Fall back to an empty object (`data ?? {}`) to preserve the previous contract.

findings.title: Custom cell renderers fall back on any falsy return, not just undefined
findings.body: Both `renderDefaultHeadCell` and `renderDefaultBodyCell` decide to use the custom renderer with `if (cell)`. The documented contract (see the prop JSDoc in `tableWidgetVisualization.tsx` and the storybook text: 'If the function returns `undefined`, fallback renderer will run') is that only `undefined` falls through. In practice a renderer that intentionally renders nothing by returning `null`, or that returns `''`/`0`/`false` for a cell value, will be silently overridden by the default renderer. Check `cell !== undefined` instead.

findings.title: Inconsistent optional chaining on required tableData prop
findings.body: `Object.keys(tableData?.meta.fields)` mixes optional chaining with a non-guarded member access and an unguarded `Object.keys`. If `tableData` is ever undefined (the surrounding code defends against it with `tableData?.data ?? []`), this throws `Cannot convert undefined or null to object` instead of rendering an empty table. Either treat `tableData` as truly required (drop the `?.`) or guard the fallback column computation.

findings.title: Analytics event recorded before feature gate and payload validation
findings.body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` is the first statement in `post()`, before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check and before schema validation. Every request from an org without the feature (which gets a 404) and every malformed request is counted as an assemble event, so the metric no longer reflects actual assemble attempts. Move the call after the feature/validation checks. Note also that with org-auth-token authentication `request.user` is anonymous, so `user_id` will be `None` for the main machine-to-machine use case.

findings.title: Unauthenticated endpoint loops over an unbounded report array
findings.body: This endpoint has `permission_classes = ()` and is CSRF exempt, yet the new code iterates the entire posted array with no cap on the number of reports: it logs the full request body, logs each invalid report (`extra={"raw_report": report}`) and emits one metric per valid report at `sample_rate=1.0`. A single large request can therefore flood logs and the metrics pipeline with attacker-controlled content. Add a maximum list length (and ideally a body size limit) before processing.

findings.title: Tests no longer exercise the application/reports+json content type
findings.body: The rewritten `test_basic` and `test_handles_multiple_reports_both_specs` post without `content_type="application/reports+json"` (the previous tests passed it explicitly). The custom `BrowserReportsJSONParser` exists precisely to accept the Browser Reporting API media type, and that is the content type real browsers send, yet it is now only covered indirectly by the negative `test_rejects_invalid_content_type` case. Keep at least one success-path test that posts with `application/reports+json`.

findings.title: Dead code left behind after removing regex experiments
findings.body: With `ParameterizationRegexExperiment` deleted, the nested `_handle_regex_match` helper inside `parametrize_w_experiments` is no longer referenced by anything (the loop now always calls `experiment.run(content, _incr_counter)`), and `ParameterizationRegex.compiled_pattern` / `_compiled_pattern` were only used by the removed class. Removing them keeps the module from accumulating unreachable branches that future readers assume are live.

findings.title: Dead `enabled` condition and default refetching on an LLM-backed endpoint
findings.body: `normalizeDateTimeParams(...)` always returns an object, so `Boolean(normalizedDateRange)` is always `true` and contributes nothing to the `enabled` guard — the intent (don't query without a date range) is not implemented. Additionally the query uses `staleTime: 5000` with default refetch behaviour, so the `/feedback-summary/` endpoint (which generates an LLM completion server-side) can be re-hit every few seconds on remount/refocus, multiplying model cost. Consider a substantially larger `staleTime` and an explicit guard on the date range.
